notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. This is an EVENT record: it stays inside the event's own inventory refs, is shorter than the prophet story that also tells the event, and refers to that story only in general words. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims; passages from several surahs are grouped by theme and surah order is not time order. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: His people said: burn him, and help your gods, if you are going to act.
In another passage the only answer of his people was to say: kill him, or burn him.
In another passage they said: build a structure for him, and throw him into the blaze.
God told the fire to be coolness and safety for Ibrahim.
They wanted to plot against him, and God made them the greatest losers.
In another passage God made them the lowest.
God saved him from the fire, and in that, God says, are signs for people who believe.

chapters.summary_md: His people said to burn Ibrahim [c1][c2], but God told the fire to be coolness and safety for him [c4]. They wanted to plot against him, and God made them the losers [c5][c7].
chapters.body_md:
His people said: burn him, and help your gods, if you are going to act [c1]. In another passage their only answer was to say: kill him, or burn him [c2], and in another they said: build a structure for him, and throw him into the blaze [c3].

God told the fire to be coolness and safety for Ibrahim [c4]. They wanted to plot against him, and God made them the greatest losers [c5]; in another passage He made them the lowest [c6]. God saved him from the fire, and in that, He says, are signs for people who believe [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The passages report the people's decision in slightly different words: burn him [c1], kill him or burn him [c2], build a structure and throw him into the blaze [c3]. The words said to the fire come in one passage only [c4], and the outcome is told in different words, greatest losers and lowest [c5][c6]. The rescue is stated in one passage, with a remark that it contains signs [c7].
chapters.kids_md: Ibrahim's people said to burn him [c1]. God told the fire to be cool and safe for Ibrahim [c4]. God saved him from the fire [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage presents the fire as acting only at God's word [c4]. Another is that the plot of Ibrahim's people ends in their own loss [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where this took place, how long the fire burned, or who built the structure.
- The verses state the command to the fire and the rescue; they do not describe Ibrahim in the fire or how he came out of it.
- Not established: whether the passages (21:68-70, 29:24, 37:97-98) describe one decision or more than one; this draft reads them together as the same event.
- Not established: how the structure and the blaze of 37:97 relate to the fire of the other passages.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on Ibrahim and the fire. None is used in this draft.
The event is also told inside the longer story of Ibrahim (content/stories/ibrahim.draft.json); this record is a shorter account that refers to it only in general words.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of the ruler, the place and the size of the fire. None is used in the story texts.
The passages are read as one event on matching wording (an inference).
The chapters group repeated passages by theme. The Quran does not give a chronology across the surahs, so the order of the chapters is a reading order only.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.
